item.title: Saudi Air Defenses intercept Houthi missiles and drones fired at Riyadh, Eastern Province
item.description: RIYADH — Saudi Air Defenses intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh. This was disclosed by Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen. He said that two drones were intercepted and destroyed in the Eastern Province.
item.dc:creator: Saudi Gazette report

item.title: Coalition intercepts Houthi drone in the vicinity of Jeddah Islamic Port
item.description: RIYADH — Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen, said that a drone, launched by the terrorist Houthi militia, was intercepted and destroyed in the vicinity of Jeddah Islamic Port."No civilians were injured as a result of falling debris from the interception of the drone,” he added.
item.dc:creator: Saudi Gazette report

item.title: Saudi transport and logistics investments set to hit SR45 billion in 2026
item.description: RIYADH — Minister of Transport and Logistics Saleh Al-Jasser said Saudi Arabia’s transport and logistics sector has made significant progress, surpassing several Saudi Vision 2030 targets ahead of schedule. He said that new investment commitments in the sector are expected to reach SR45 billion in 2026, despite regional challenges.Speaking at a panel discussion titled "Logistical and technical capabilities connecting the world" at the Budget 2027 Forum in Riyadh on Wednesday, Al-Jasser said…

item.title: PIF secures inaugural S&P A+ credit rating with stable outlook
item.description: RIYADH — The Public Investment Fund (PIF) announced on Wednesday that S&P Global Ratings has assigned its inaugural A+ long-term foreign and local currency issuer credit ratings, with a stable outlook. PIF’s existing A-1 short-term rating remains unchanged, with PIF’s ratings in line with those of Saudi Arabia.The A+ rating reflects confidence in PIF’s long-term strategy and its strong financial position. item.title: Houthi projectile hits Jazan port, no injuries reported
item.description: RIYADH — A projectile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia fell at Jazan port, causing minor damage but no civilian casualties. Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen, stated that efforts were underway to determine the type of projectile used.
item.dc:creator: Saudi Gazette report
